Subject: Dedicated throughput guarantees — what does Redwood measure?

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Our procurement team asked for a clear statement on the throughput guarantees we can expect under a Dedicated/GPU-pool commit. Specifically they want: tokens/sec (aggregate across pool), requests/sec (concurrency assumptions), and how you measure these numbers for acceptance and billing.

Two quick constraints from our side:
- Typical prompt lengths avg ~120 tokens, but tail goes to 2k for a small percentage (~2%).
- We need 99th-percentile latency under 450ms for single-turn text-gen (non-streaming) for requests <= 512 tokens.

Can you send a short proposal that includes: measurement methodology, a reproducible acceptance harness (or script), what counts as a throughput failure, and what credits/penalties look like? Procurement needs this to review the SOW.

Appreciate it — we’re trying to finalize the commit band this week.

Best,
Sylvia

Sylvia — thanks, great questions. I pulled together a concise proposal and attached a draft terms doc for procurement to review (Dedicated_Guarantee_Terms_draft_v1.pdf). High-level summary below, followed by the acceptance steps we recommend.

High-level guarantee (example band):
- Commit band: 100M tokens/month reserved on a 3-month term (example).
- Throughput guarantee: 12,000 tokens/sec (aggregate pool) sustained for a 1-hour rolling window under the agreed workload profile.
- Concurrency guidance: assumes average concurrent requests of 60 with average prompt length 120 tokens; see acceptance harness for exact request mix.
- Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for requests <= 512 tokens (single-turn, non-streaming).

Measurement & acceptance methodology (short):
1) Define workload spec (prompt length distribution, concurrency, rate shape) — we recommend you run with your representative prompt set; if not available, use our supplied synthetic mix.
2) Run a 2-stage acceptance: baseline warm-up (30m, autoscale allowed) then a 1-hour measurement window where metrics are collected in 10s buckets.
3) Tokens/sec measured as the sum of generated tokens across all workers divided by wall-clock time within the measurement window (exclude warm-up).
4) Latency computed at request-level, p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end response completion (network+inference). Requests outside <=512 tokens are excluded from that latency SLO.
5) Outlier handling: drop top and bottom 0.5% of buckets to avoid pump artifacts; if >5% of requests exceed latency SLO, crediting triggers.

Credits & remediation matrix (summary):
- If measured throughput >= 95% of guarantee and p95 latency within target: no credit.
- If throughput between 80–95% or p95 slightly above target: partial credit (pro-rata for deficit).
- If throughput < 80% or p95 > target by >20%: full service credit for affected window and joint runbook to remediate.

I’ve copied Ben (pricing) to propose commit bands/discounts and Karthik (SRE) for the harness and test repo. If you’re OK, we can schedule a 30-min run-through with procurement and your infra team early next week.

-jasmine

Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — measurement harness details

Sylvia — quick technical note on measurement so procurement can see reproducibility details.

We maintain an acceptance harness (linked in thread) that runs increasingly realistic workloads. Key points:
- Workload driver: multi-threaded gRPC client that can replay prompt sets with timestamped traces. Supports: fixed-rate, ramp, and burst profiles.
- Measurement window: 60 minutes with 10s buckets; tokens/sec reported as mean and median across buckets plus min/max.
- Warm-up: 30 minutes to populate KV cache and stabilise autoscaling; we do not include warm-up in acceptance metrics.
- Accounting for partial responses: generator tokens are counted only when a 200 OK is returned; preempted or errored requests fail the window unless under a configured maintenance window.
- Network normalization: tests should run from your prod VPC (preferred) or our test agents in the same region; network RTT below 10ms is assumed for the latency SLO. If your RTT is higher, we provide network-adjusted targets.

Runbook snippet we propose to include in the SOW:
- If acceptance fails, do a joint investigation window (2 business days) with shared traces.
- If issue is infra/capacity on Redwood side, remediation and credits per table in the draft terms.

I pushed a small example harness to the repo: /kairos-acceptance/examples/short-run.md (link in metadata). Happy to walk your infra folks through setup.

—Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Sylvia — looping in pricing details as requested. Below are illustrative commit bands and the discount structure. These are flexible; we can lock in at different bands with step-down pricing.

Example commit bands (monthly tokens, USD list price reference):
- Band A: 50M tokens/month — baseline price $X/token — 12% discount with 12-month commit
- Band B: 150M tokens/month — 18% discount with 12-month commit
- Band C: 300M tokens/month — 24% discount + reserved capacity priority (preferred scheduling)

Throughput ties & acceptance:
- Each band will have a corresponding throughput guarantee (scaled): e.g. Band B -> 18,000 tokens/sec aggregate sustained as measured in the 1-hour window. We adjust guarantees for model size & quantization used.
- If acceptance reveals a mismatch in the workload (e.g., heavier tails), we include a one-time adjustment window to recalibrate targets before finalizing SOW.

Crediting mechanics (commercial):
- Credits are calculated pro-rata based on shortfall: (Guarantee - Observed) / Guarantee * monthly commit value for the affected measurement period, capped at 30% of monthly commit.

If you can confirm a target band (A/B/C) this week, we’ll update the SOW and circulate a DocuSign route.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Thanks all. A few clarifying items from procurement & infra:
1) Our infra team wants the p99 latency metric included in the SOW for the allocation; they know p95 is useful but p99 is the tail they see in production. Can you provide an adjusted table for p99 targets (and whether they carry the same crediting thresholds)?
2) The network normalization: our VPC egress has ~18–20ms median RTT to Redwood agents in us-west — that suggests we may need an adjusted latency target. Can you send the network-adjusted SLO table?
3) On credits: procurement asked whether credits are cash-equivalent or account credit — preference for account credit with rollover is okay.

Also: can we get a short call (15–20m) to run through the acceptance harness next Tue? Prefer 10:00–11:00 PT.

-sylvia

Sylvia — thanks for the notes. Attached is a short redline to the draft terms (see Drive link). Quick answers and next steps:
- p99: we can include p99 as an informational metric; we recommend keeping crediting tied to p95 to avoid severe sensitivity to transient tails. However, if you prefer, we can make p99 a secondary crediting trigger with a higher threshold (e.g., p99 > target by 30% triggers review, >50% triggers credit).
- Network: we’ll produce a network-adjusted table (based on measured RTT) — if your median RTT is 18–20ms we propose adding 15–20ms buffer to the SLO so that service-levels reflect only inference time. We’ll write the exact table into the SOW.
- Credits: account credit with 6-month rollover is acceptable; we’ll state that in the draft.

Proposed next steps:
1) 15-min run-through of the harness on Tue 10:30 PT (we’ll send invite).
2) Redwood to produce network-adjusted SLO table + revised redline by EOD Tue.
3) Procurement to confirm preferred commit band (A/B/C) so we can finalize pricing sheet.

If that works I’ll update the Drive copy and route DocuSign once procurement signs off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
